issue.title: Epic: Album ranker MVP
issue.body:
Replace the "Best Albums" spreadsheet with an app where the user searches an album catalog, ranks favorites per year with cover art, and gets artist and decade lists from Elo ratings built from yearly ranks and head-to-head matchups. The requirements are settled in #2; the other tickets build what it describes.

This epic is a container. The team builds its child tickets, not the epic itself.

## Tickets

* #2 Write the MVP requirements spec for the album ranking app (first; the build tickets follow it)
* #3 Choose the tech stack and scaffold the app
* #4 Define the data model and storage for albums, years and rankings
* #5 Add album catalog search with cover art
* #6 Build the per-year ranking screen with drag and drop and covers
* #7 Build the Elo rating engine and matchup screen
* #8 Add artist views by decade and overall
* #9 Add decade top 25 album lists
* #10 Import the existing spreadsheet
* #14 Deploy the app to AWS with staging and production behind a password gate

issue.title: Add local preview environments for main and per-ticket branches
issue.body:
Make it a documented, repeatable step to run the app locally in two ways: a main preview built from the `main` branch, and a preview of any ticket's branch on its own local port, side by side.

## Today
- The only documented way to run the app is `npm run dev` on port 3000 from one checkout (README "Run the app"). Nothing says how to preview a branch next to main.
- Ticket branches already live in separate git worktrees (`git worktree list` shows one per ticket under `~/.t3/worktrees/album-ranker/`), but nothing starts the app from them.
- `package.json` has `dev`, `build` and `start` scripts that take Next's default port. No script or doc sets a port.
- The SQLite path comes from `DATABASE_PATH` in `lib/config.ts`, defaulting to `./data/album-ranker.db` relative to the working directory. A worktree gets its own `data/` folder by default, which is gitignored. Nothing documents this or how a preview should seed data.
- `.env*` is gitignored except `.env.example`, so each checkout needs its own `.env`.

## Scope
- Main preview: a documented command or script that runs the app from the `main` branch (root checkout, which stays on `main`) on a fixed port, and how to refresh it after a merge.
- Ticket preview: a documented command or script that takes a ticket number or branch, finds its worktree, and runs the app from it on a different local port. Several ticket previews can run at once.
- Port scheme: one fixed port for main and a rule for choosing a ticket's port, so two previews never collide. Fail with a clear message when a port is taken.
- Data: each preview uses its own `DATABASE_PATH`, so a branch's migrations never touch the main preview's data. Say how to start empty or copy the main file.
- Setup per worktree is covered: install dependencies and create `.env` when missing.
- A way to stop a preview.
- Document it in the README, and note it in `docs/agents/project.md` § Environments and deploy.

## Acceptance
- One command starts the main preview on its fixed port, serving `main`.
- One command per ticket starts a preview of that ticket's branch on a different port while the main preview keeps running.
- Changing data in a ticket preview does not change the main preview's data.
- The README steps work from a fresh checkout with a ticket worktree.
- Nothing from `data/` or `.env` is committed.

## Out of scope
- Deploying the app anywhere (see #14).
- Browser test runs and event capture (see #19).
- A shared or hosted preview URL, and CI preview builds.

issue.title: feat: ALBUM-7 Elo rating engine and matchup screen
issue.body:
Closes #7

Ticket: [ALBUM-7](https://github.com/dbeallor/album-ranker/issues/7). Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-21-album-7-elo-matchup.md`. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-21-album-7-elo-matchup.md`.

Adds the Elo rating engine (`lib/elo/`, pure: update, replay with implied results, artist score, matchup picking), a loader and answer/skip/undo logic (`lib/ratings.ts`, `lib/matchups-service.ts`), and the `/matchups` screen. Ratings are replayed on each request and never stored. No schema changes.

## Proof

- **A wins between two new albums gives 1516 / 1484; a 1500 v 1500 tie changes nothing; replay is deterministic**: `lib/elo/elo.test.ts` (table) and `lib/elo/replay.test.ts` pass.

  ```
  $ npx vitest run lib/elo lib/matchups-service components/matchup-screen
   Test Files  6 passed (6)
        Tests  58 passed (58)
  ```

- **Implied results are exactly ranked over lower ranked and over honorable mention**: `impliedResults` test in `lib/elo/replay.test.ts` (fixture year with ranks 1, 2, 4, honorable mentions and a listed album).
- **Answering changes both ratings; undo restores them exactly**: `lib/matchups-service.test.ts` ("an answer moves both ratings", "undo restores the ratings exactly"), against an in-memory database; `replay.test.ts` covers the same at the engine level.
- **Never same-year, listed, or already-played pair while an unplayed one exists**: `lib/elo/pick.test.ts` and "never serves a listed or unplaced album" in `lib/matchups-service.test.ts`; the answer action refuses same-year, listed, unplaced and unknown pairs and stores nothing.
- **Artist score of albums rated 1600 and 1700 is 1600**: `lib/elo/artist-score.test.ts`.
- **Screen covered by a component test**: `components/matchup-screen.test.tsx` (pick, tie, skip, undo, counter, undo disabled at zero).

  ```
  $ npm test && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run build
  Tests  131 passed (131)   (lint and typecheck: no output; build compiled, /matchups is dynamic)
  ```

Not proven:
- The screen in a real browser: no browser test setup in the repo, and `/matchups` has no data to show until albums can be added to years (#6) or imported (#10). No screenshot.

Context size: pass skipped (not collective-wisdom)
